title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from §6). Σ is an abstract graded ring, the model being the ring of cohomological correspondences End(H^*(X)) for a smooth projective X of dimension n. L ∈ Σ^(2) is a Lefschetz element. The π_i ∈ Σ^(0) are the degree projectors. The π_{i,α} are the projectors of the Lefschetz decomposition. For i ≤ n, π_{i,α} projects onto L^α P^{i-2α}, where P^k is the primitive part in degree k. For degrees 2n-i ≥ n, Grothendieck indexes from the dual side: π_{2n-i,α} = L^{n-i} π_{i,α} Λ^{n-i} (6.14 ④), the piece L^{n-i}L^α P^{i-2α}. Λ ∈ Σ^(-2) is the 'canonical' inverse Lefschetz operator in Kleiman's normalisation: Λ(L^α x) = L^{α-1}x for x primitive and α ≥ 1, and Λx = 0 for x primitive.

Formula (6.15). The previous page gives eight conditions (6.14) that characterise Λ and the π_{i,α} uniquely in terms of L and the π_i. Here the last four conditions (⑤–⑧) are replaced by two:
- LΛ = 1 − Σ_{0≤i≤n} π_{i,0}, i.e. 1 minus the projection onto the primitive classes;
- ΛL = 1 − Σ_{n≤j≤2n} π_{j,0}, i.e. 1 minus the projection onto the 'coprimitive' classes L^{n-k}P^k, the tops of the Lefschetz strings, which L kills.
The check is immediate. On L^α x with x primitive of degree k, LΛ is the identity if α ≥ 1 and zero if α = 0. ΛL is the identity unless α = n−k, where L^{α+1}x = 0. The degree-n primitive projector π_{n,0} correctly appears in both sums.

The crossed-out and reworked paragraph announces the aim: express the π_i, Λ, L by relations purely inside the abstract graded ring Σ. A margin note says 'cf n° 7 pour l'anneau Φ : explicit[ation] des relations'.

Section 7. The aim is to find a universal model in which these relations can be read off. Take a free Z-module M_0 of rank 2n with a non-degenerate alternating form ξ_0 ∈ Λ²M_0, stressed as unimodular 'sur Z !'. Let ξ* ∈ Λ²M_0^∨ be the dual form and M_0^* = ΛM_0 the exterior algebra; this is the integral cohomology of a principally polarised abelian variety, or of a 2n-torus. Define L_0 = ξ_0 ∧ (wedge with ξ_0) and Λ_0 = ξ* ⌟ (contraction with ξ*). Then Φ_0 = Z[L_0, Λ_0] ⊂ End_Z(M_0^*) is the subring they generate. He notes that End(M^*), acting presumably on M^*_Q, with L satisfies the hard Lefschetz condition (6.1)(ii), and relates Λ_0 to the canonical Λ of (6.15).

The next page abstracts this into a free Z-algebra 𝔏 with basis of matrix units φ_i^{β,α}, multiplying by φ_i^{β,α}φ_{i'}^{β',α'} = δ φ. So 𝔏 ≅ ∏_{i=0}^{n} M_{n−i+1}(Z), one matrix ring per primitive degree acting on its Lefschetz string. A proposition follows: a graded M^* satisfies the Lefschetz conditions iff there is a ring homomorphism 𝔏 → End sending the universal L to L. In other words, 𝔏 is the universal 'Lefschetz ring' over Z in which L, Λ, π_i, π_{i,α} live with integral structure constants. The purpose is the standard conjectures: show that Λ, and the Künneth/Lefschetz projectors, lie in any graded subring of correspondences that contains L and the π_i and satisfies Lefschetz.
errors: Λ_0 = contraction with ξ* is the sl2-partner of L_0, not Grothendieck's canonical Λ of (6.15). On L^α x with x primitive of degree k one gets Λ_0(L^α x) = α(n−k−α+1)·L^{α−1}x (up to sign convention), whereas the canonical Λ gives L^{α−1}x. So Λ_0 equals the canonical Λ only up to these rational scalars on isotypic pieces. The canonical Λ lies in Φ_0⊗Q, but it is not clear that it lies in Φ_0 = Z[L_0,Λ_0] itself. If the page asserts that Λ_0 is the canonical operation of (6.15), that is inaccurate.

Over Z, L_0^{n−i}: Λ^i M_0 → Λ^{2n−i} M_0 is not an isomorphism for n−i ≥ 2. For example ξ∧ξ = 2·(volume form) when n = 2, so divided powers ξ^{[k]} are needed. Hard Lefschetz (6.1)(ii) therefore holds only after tensoring with Q. This is consistent with the marginal 'opérant sur M^*_Q' (probable reading) but clashes with the emphasis on working over Z.
Next page: the index range 0≤α,β≤2n−i for φ_i^{β,α} should be 0≤α,β≤n−i, the length of the Lefschetz string of a primitive class of degree i.

ideas.what: Characterisation of the canonical Λ by LΛ = 1 − (primitive projector) and ΛL = 1 − (coprimitive projector)
ideas.modern_name: Kleiman-normalised Lefschetz inverse Λ (standard conjecture B operator)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Standard conjectures (1969); Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968)
ideas.where_published: Λ appears in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/69); this exact pair of identities is not recalled there

ideas.what: Exterior algebra of a unimodular symplectic Z-lattice with L = ∧ξ, Λ = ξ*⌟ as universal model of a Lefschetz structure
ideas.modern_name: cohomology of a principally polarised abelian variety as sl2/Lefschetz model; Lefschetz (Looijenga–Lunts) modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lieberman (1968) and Kleiman for standard conjecture B for abelian varieties; Looijenga–Lunts (1997) for Lie-algebraic Lefschetz modules

ideas.what: Universal Z-algebra 𝔏 ≅ ∏ M_{n−i+1}(Z) of matrix units encoding the Lefschetz decomposition, with modules over it equivalent to graded objects satisfying Lefschetz (next page)
ideas.modern_name: integral Lefschetz algebra / Z-form of the image of U(sl2) on ⊕V_{n−i}

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an integral 'universal Lefschetz ring' (Φ_0 = Z[L_0,Λ_0] inside the exterior algebra of a unimodular symplectic lattice, abstracted to 𝔏) to obtain intrinsic ring-theoretic relations defining Λ and the Lefschetz projectors inside any graded correspondence ring. The comparison over Z between Z[L_0, contraction] and the canonical Λ, which lies in 𝔏, is left unresolved, and the integrality question (divided powers) is not addressed.
missed.quote: considérons l'algèbre Φ_0 = Z[L_0, Λ_0] ⊂ End_Z(M_0^*) ... Λ_0 est l'opération canonique définie par (6.15)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and torsion versions of the standard conjectures (Lefschetz type over Z, integral Künneth/Lefschetz projectors) are of current interest. A precise comparison of Z-forms of the Lefschetz algebra could clarify which denominators are unavoidable.

missed.claim: Using abelian-variety cohomology as the universal source of the polynomial relations for Λ anticipates the mechanism of Lieberman's proof of B(A) for abelian varieties. Grothendieck aims to transport those relations to arbitrary X.
missed.quote: Partons pour ceci d'un module libre M de rang 2n sur Z, muni d'une 2-forme alternée (sur Z !) non dégénérée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modest. It is a known circle of ideas (Lieberman, Kleiman, later Looijenga–Lunts, André), but this 'universal ring' formulation is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The (6.15) identities are routine. The integral universal Lefschetz ring 𝔏 / Φ_0 built from a unimodular symplectic lattice is a tidy, apparently unpublished formulation. Its ideas are close to Kleiman–Lieberman's treatment of conjecture B, so a specialist would find it natural rather than startling.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note near 'opérant sur M^*_Z' more plausibly reads 'opérant sur M^*_Q' (a ℚ-like subscript), consistent with hard Lefschetz holding only rationally.
Margin note at left reads roughly 'cf n° 7 pour l'anneau Φ : explicit[ation] des relations ...'.
The opening line of §7 likely reads 'Revenant à la situation d'un L ∈ Σ^(2)', not 'Revenant au cas'.
The dual form note reads 'ξ* ∈ Λ²M_0^∨ la forme duale' and Λ_0 x = ξ_0^* ⌟ x (contraction).
Page number in corner is 11 (archive page 13).
